actions.justification: Mandatory first step. Patient has tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnea, and hypoxia - all concerning for significant PE. Formal vital sign assessment establishes baseline and severity.

Mandatory. Wells score is the primary clinical decision tool for PE probability. This patient has multiple high-risk features: signs of DVT (leg swelling), PE most likely diagnosis, tachycardia, immobilization (long-haul flight), and OCP use - expected high probability score.

Mandatory. D-dimer is essential in the PE diagnostic workup per ESC guidelines. In conjunction with Wells score, guides need for CT pulmonary angiography. Must be ordered urgently given time-critical presentation.
Patient has SpO2 of 92%, which is below the acceptable threshold of 94%. Supplemental oxygen is immediately indicated to correct hypoxia per ESC PE guidelines and basic supportive care principles.

12-lead ECG should be obtained promptly to evaluate for right heart strain patterns (S1Q3T3, new RBBB, sinus tachycardia) consistent with PE, and to exclude STEMI or other arrhythmias as per AHA chest pain and ESC PE guidelines. Tachycardia and hemodynamic compromise make this a priority.

Chest X-ray is part of the initial workup for suspected PE to evaluate for alternative diagnoses (pneumothorax, pneumonia, pleural effusion) and baseline cardiopulmonary status. Patient has hypoxia (SpO2 92%) and tachypnea (RR 24) requiring urgent assessment.

Echocardiogram is indicated in suspected high-risk/intermediate-risk PE to assess right ventricular dysfunction (RV strain), which guides risk stratification and treatment intensity. Patient has tachycardia (HR 112), hypotension (BP 108/68), and hypoxia suggesting possible intermediate-high risk PE.

CT pulmonary angiography is the gold-standard imaging for confirming pulmonary embolism per ESC PE guidelines. This patient has high pre-test probability (pleuritic chest pain, leg swelling, tachycardia, hypoxia, OCP use, recent long-haul flight) and requires definitive imaging to confirm diagnosis and guide anticoagulation decisions.

A 12-lead ECG should be obtained per AHA chest pain guidelines within 10 minutes of presentation to evaluate for S1Q3T3 pattern, right heart strain, sinus tachycardia, or STEMI. Although order_ecg is completed, order_imaging_ecg is a distinct available action_id and may provide formal ECG interpretation for PE risk stratification.

Given high clinical suspicion for PE with hemodynamic compromise (HR 112, BP 108/68, SpO2 92%), empiric anticoagulation with unfractionated heparin is indicated per ESC PE guidelines before imaging confirmation when pretest probability is high and there is no contraindication, to prevent clot propagation while awaiting CT-PA results.
Patient has SpO2 92% and RR 24 — ABG will quantify degree of hypoxemia, hypocapnia, and acid-base status, which helps risk-stratify PE severity and guide oxygen/ventilation decisions.
Patient has leg swelling after long-haul flight; lower extremity DVT Doppler confirms proximal DVT, supports PE diagnosis, and informs duration of anticoagulation therapy.

With tachycardia (HR 112), hypotension borderline (BP 108/68), and SpO2 92%, bedside echocardiogram is critical to assess right ventricular dysfunction/strain, which determines whether this is a high-risk (massive) PE requiring thrombolysis versus intermediate-risk PE managed with anticoagulation alone.
CBC is needed to assess for anemia, thrombocytopenia, or leukocytosis which may affect PE management and anticoagulation decisions.
BNP helps assess right heart strain/dysfunction, which is critical for risk stratification of PE severity (massive vs submassive).
BMP assesses renal function (important for contrast clearance post CT-PA and anticoagulation dosing), electrolytes, and metabolic status in this hemodynamically borderline patient.
Troponin is essential in PE risk stratification to assess right ventricular myocardial injury. Elevated troponin indicates higher-risk PE and influences management decisions.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT) are needed to monitor anticoagulation therapy already initiated with heparin and to assess baseline coagulation status.
Patient has borderline hemodynamics (BP 108/68, MAP 81) with tachycardia and hypoxia. Lactate will help assess tissue perfusion and guide escalation decisions including vasopressors or thrombolysis.

Patient has confirmed/suspected PE with hemodynamic compromise (HR 112, BP 108/68, SpO2 92%). Anticoagulation is the cornerstone of PE treatment per ESC guidelines. Heparin has been given but ongoing anticoagulation management is needed.
Patient has intermediate-to-high risk PE features (tachycardia, hypotension, hypoxia, RR 24). Pulmonology consultation warranted for co-management and guidance on escalation of therapy.
LMWH is an evidence-based anticoagulation option for PE management per ESC guidelines, appropriate for this patient with suspected PE and no contraindications listed.

Patient has borderline hypotension (BP 108/68, MAP 81) with tachycardia (HR 112) and signs of hemodynamic compromise from PE. Cautious IV fluid bolus (250-500mL) can support RV preload and improve cardiac output in PE with hypotension, per ESC PE guidelines for hemodynamically unstable PE.

Patient has low BP (108/68) with tachycardia and SpO2 92%, suggesting intermediate-high or high-risk PE with hemodynamic compromise. Vasopressors (e.g., norepinephrine) may be needed to maintain perfusion pressure if fluid resuscitation is insufficient, per ESC PE guidelines for shock/hypotension in PE.
